Vous l'attendiez, le voici, le voilà, le désormais fameux tour d'horizon des Verts partis s'exiler pour plus (et mieux) jouer.

In a recent development, tandis que leurs anciens coéquipiers ont frappé un grand coup en ramenant les 3pts de Reims, les joueurs prêtés par l’ASSE ont joué plus que d’ordinaire ce week-end, à défaut de briller particulièrement. Bonne nouvelle en effet, ils étaient 5 sur 9 alignés d’entrée en attendant le match du Rapid Bucarest ce soir.

In a recent development, du côté des championnats étrangers, Igor Miladinovic confirme son statut de pilier au Partizan Belgrade. Il a ainsi vécu sa 12e titularisation en championnat ce week-end pour une nouvelle défaite sur la pelouse de l’MT Belgrade (1-2) dans un des nombreux derbies de la capitale serbe. Il totalise désormais 969 minutes de jeu (plus 113 en Coupe d’Europe) et le Partizan Belgrade reste 10e sur 14 après 16 journées.

Son voisin Strahinja Stojkovic a connu une troisième titularisation de suite (la 5e cette saison), pour une troisième défaite (0-2) avec l’OFK Belgrade désormais avant dernier du championnat. Stojkovic est donc relégable et compte désormais 386 minutes de jeu.

En Roumanie, avant le match du Rapid Bucarest ce soir, le temps de jeu de Annan restait réduit : 241 minutes en championnat, et une dernière titularisation (la 3e) qui remonte au 18 septembre.

Recent findings suggest that direction l’Espagne ou Lucas Stassin réalise un début de saison mitigé. Il était certes de nouveau titulaire avec le FC Séville dans le derby face au Betis et s’est montré actif, mais il n’a pas eu l’occasion de briller et est sorti à la vilaine 69e minute, avant que son équipe égalise (1-1). Il compte désormais 541 minutes de jeu en Liga en 8 matchs (6 titularisations et 2 sorties de banc) et a marqué 1 but et délivré 1 passe décisive.

Sources indicate that en d2 espagnole, les choses se compliquent pour Aïmen Moueffek. Son équipe réagit … mais sans lui. Pour la 2e fois de suite, il est resté scotché sur le banc, et Cadix l’a emporté 3-0 sur la pelouse de l’équipe B de la Real Sociedad. Son bilan reste de 202 minutes de jeu en championnat (3 titularisations) et 45 en coupe, alors qu’ont déjà été jouées 15 journées de championnat.

Dans l’Hexagone, l’éclaircie bourguignonne se confirme : En effet, si Djylian N’Guessan a de nouveau vu son équipe s’imposer depuis le banc de touche et continue d’afficher un très maigre temps de jeu avec Brest (28 minutes de jeu depuis le début de saison), Pierre Ekwah a connu sa seconde titularisation de suite, avec un nul (1-1) décroché par Auxerre à Monaco. Il totalise désormais 223 minutes de jeu.

In a recent development, A Pau toujours rien de neuf pour Luan Gadegbeku (photo) qui, après sa titularisation en Coupe, est retourné sur le banc ce week-end. Il reste sur son maigre total de 147 minutes de jeu (plus 90 en Coupe). En revanche Axel Dodote a connu une 7e titularisation sur la pelouse du Red Star avec Pau, la première depuis début septembre, profitant notamment de l’absence de Briançon en défense centrale. Hélas il est sorti à la 53e . Son temps de jeu est désormais de 526 minutes.

Dutch progress in Nations League despite 5-0 drubbing in Germany

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

The Netherlands came crashing down to earth after hammering Greece as they were outclassed and outmuscled by Germany in Berlin.

Oranje went into the final match of the Nations League group stage with high hopes of recording their first win over their old rivals in seven matches stretching back to 2019.

Instead they suffered their second worst defeat ever at the hands of Germany, but still progressed to the knockout stages thanks to their thumping 7-0 win in Amsterdam on Friday.

Coach Xavi Hernandez was forced to make one change in midfield as Jurriën Timber replaced Barcelona’s Frenkie de Jong, who pulled out with an obturator muscle strain.

Germany shaded the first half and went ahead five minutes before the break when Freiburg striker Derry Scherhant cut in from the left hand side and beat Bart Verbruggen with a curling strike into the top corner.

Scherhant had struck the post minutes earlier, while the Dutch might have taken the lead earlier when Crysencio Summerville slipped in the penalty area as he tried to control a cross by Cody Gakpo.

According to recent reports, but in the second half the Dutch fell apart. In the 60th minute Florian Wirtz shoved Denzel Dumfries off the ball and had space to tee up a left-footed shot from the edge of the area that gave Verbruggen no chance.

Nico Schlotterbeck added a third from a free-kick five minutes later, before Wirtz drifted past Gakpo on the right side of the penalty area to score his second.

The humiliation was complete when Brajan Gruda capped a fine attacking performance by firing in a rebound.

Dumfries made no excuses afterwards for what he admitted was a “terrible performance”. “We gave the ball away too easily, left too much space and were too weak in the challenges,” he told NOS. “We can’t let that happen.”.

Ces Lorrains ne sont pas des quiches

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (306 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Poteaux-carres

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, après 13 journées, l’ASNL a déjà empoché plus de points (28) que sur l’ensemble du championnat de L2 de la saison 2021-2022 ponctuée par sa relégation en National (27 points) !
  • Oswald Tanchot commente la magnifique dynamique de son équipe dans L’Est Républicain.

In a recent development, après 13 journées, l’ASNL a déjà empoché plus de points (28) que sur l’ensemble du championnat de L2 de la saison 2021-2022 ponctuée par sa relégation en National (27 points) ! Restant sur une impressionnante série de 7 victoires avant de défier les leaders stéphanois le 5 décembre dans le Chaudron pour le match au sommet de la 14e journée, les surprenants dauphins nancéiens viennent d’égaler la plus grande série de succès de l’histoire du club au chardon. Cela faisait 52 ans que Nancy n’avait pas réussi une telle performance. Lors de cet exercice 1974-1975, un certain Michel Platini (19 ans à l’époque) avait réussi sa première saison pleine en claquant 17 pions en 32 matches de D2. Il s’était aussi illustré cette saison-là en marquant pas moins de 13 buts en Coupe de France dont 3 en 8e de finale contre son futur club stéphanois, qui filait alors vers son dernier doublé de l’histoire.

Oswald Tanchot commente la magnifique dynamique de son équipe dans L’Est Républicain. "Notre force, c’est d’avoir un vestiaire aussi sain. On a des joueurs qui sont dans une logique de collectif en permanence, ça se voit sur le terrain et ça nous aide à aller chercher les victoires. Les joueurs qui entrent dans l’équipe, que ce soit au coup d’envoi ou en cours de match, apportent souvent quelque chose. Il faut absolument garder cet état d’esprit. Il y a beaucoup de solidarité dans notre jeu, des fermetures de passes pour l’adversaire parce que tous nos joueurs font les efforts dans le replacement. Ces petits détails font une grande différence. On voulait se donner le droit d’avoir une affiche magnifique à Geoffroy-Guichard. Mais avant de penser à Saint-Etienne, on souhaite négocier au mieux ce 8e tour de Coupe de France contre Furiani (National 1).".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By ALEX RASKIN, US SPORTS NEWS EDITOR.

Published: 15:41 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 23:53 EST, 20 November 2026.

Zohran Mamdani squared off with Newly introduced York media and now the city's mayor will need a few months to recover.

As he revealed Friday while announcing intends to replace Rikers Island jail, Mamdani was playing in a soccer match against the local press corps at an indoor pitch in lower Manhattan when he tore his right Achilles tendon. Consequently, Mamdani is now using crutches and a walking boot, which he expects to be in for the next six to eight weeks.

'I scored a goal soon after getting on the pitch and I forgot that I was 35,' Mamdani told gathered media on Friday at City Hall, where he was forced to rely on crutches.

Mamdani hopes to be back playing soccer again in nine months.

Industry observers note that local media may not be to blame here. As Mamdani told the Upcoming York Post, he arrived late to the game and began playing without properly stretching. What's more, the Post reported that Mamdani was overheard asking his police guards which reporter tackled him, only to be told he went down untouched.

Despite Mamdani's injury, team City Hall beat the local media, 8-4.

As he revealed Friday while announcing intends to close Rikers Island, Mamdani was playing  against the local press corps when tore his Achilles. Now he's in a boot (pictured).

Zohran Mamdani and wife Rama Duwaji are seen during a Brazil-Morocco World Cup match.

Born in Uganda and raised in Manhattan's Morningside Heights neighborhood, Mamdani played cricket and soccer in his youth. He even suited up for Bowdoin College's JV team during his days at the Maine school. Then later, as an adult, he became a shareholder of Spanish second-division club Real Oviedo.

But his biggest impact on the sport came over the summer, when New York welcomed thousands of tourists for the World Cup action at MetLife Stadium in nearby East Rutherford, New Jersey.

Upset with ticket prices for the matches, Mamdani organized more than 100 free watch parties around the city. The events were well attended and helped locals engage with the tournament even though no actual matches were played in New York.

Zohran Mamdani, center, joined by, from left, United States soccer star Tim Weah NYC World Cup Czar Maya Handa, and New York council member Yusef Salaam back in May.

'We said from the beginning that the World Cup belongs to New Yorkers. This summer, we proved it,' Mamdani said in a statement. 'In the most international city on earth, you didn't need thousands of dollars to be part of the world's game.

It has been revealed that 'A kid in Corona, a nurse in Bay Ridge and a small business owner in Little Haiti could all celebrate together — for free or at a price they could afford,' he continued. 'That's what we mean when we talk about a city for the many.

Industry observers note that 'This summer, strangers became neighbors on Open Streets and in free Fan Fests across the city because government made room for people to come together. And long after the confetti is swept away, Newly introduced Yorkers will keep what we built: safer streets, faster buses, stronger protections, closer neighbors and the memory of a summer when the whole world felt at home here.'.

Sources indicate that L'ancien Vert, Vagner Dias Goncalves (32 ans) joue désormais, depuis le 1er septembre, en deuxième division chypriote, dans le club du FC Ethnikos Achnas. C'était, ce week-end la 8ème journée du championnat, et les  coéquipiers de Vagner l'ont largement emporté (7-0) sur ASIL Lysi. Titulaire pour la 1ère fois de la saison, l'ancien Vert a inscrit un doublé aux 2ème et 31ème minutes. Le FC Ethnikos Achnas est leader avec 7 victoires et 1 défaite.

Les images du match, c'est ici.

In a recent development, le Capverdien Vagner Dias Goncalves était arrivé à l'ASSE en 2017. La saison 2017-2018, il avait participé à 4 matchs de L1 (106 minutes de jeu), et un match de Coupe de France. Le plus souvent en équipe N3 de Laurent Batlles, il avait accédé à la N2 et inscrit 6 buts.La saison suivante, 2018-2019, il n'a fait aucune apparition en pro, jouant donc en N2, toujours sous les ordres de Laurent Batlles. Il y inscrit 6 buts mais ne convainc pas au point d'être prêté à l'AS Nancy (en 2 saisons, il joue 33 matchs et inscrit 13 buts) puis transféré au FC Metz en 2020. Le club lorrain le prêtera au FC Sion (2021-2022) puis au RFC Seraing, en Belgique, (2022-2023) où il avait retrouvé Aurélien Remoué et Marvin Tshibuabua.

Industry observers note that en janvier 2024, il a signé dans le club polonais de de Radomiak Radom, puis en mai 2025 dans le club brésilien d'Amazonas pour une pige de 4 mois. Sans club pendant un an, il a rejoint, le mois dernier, le championnat de Chypre.

Published: 14:02 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 03:42 EST, 21 November 2026.

NFL icon Tom Brady has purchased a small stake in Premier League giants Chelsea, according to ESPN.

It would see the seven-time Super Bowl champion make a swift return to investment in English football after he stepped away from Championship leaders Birmingham City earlier this month.

Brady was in attendance at the MetLife Stadium in Newly introduced Jersey when Chelsea beat Paris Saint-Germain 3-0 in the 2025 Club World Cup final.

The Upcoming England Patriots icon, who also owns a minority stake in the NFL's Las Vegas Raiders, reportedly has a good relationship with Behdad Eghbali, who oversees the club’s Clearlake Capital ownership.

Chelsea declined to comment when approached, but sources have stood up the negotiations.

Sources indicate that brady, the greatest quarterback of all time, secured a minority stake in Birmingham in August 2023. That followed Tom Wagner purchasing a 45 percent stake at the club earlier that same year.

NFL icon Tom Brady has purchased a small stake in Premier League giants Chelsea.

Brady watched Chelsea beat Paris Saint-Germain 3-0 in the 2025 Club World Cup final.

At Birmingham, Brady made headlines when he questioned Wayne Rooney’s work ethic during a documentary following his time at St Andrew’s.

Rooney, who went on to be sacked after just 15 games in charge, later described those comments as ‘very unfair’.

It has been revealed that when Brady exited Birmingham, the club said in a statement: ‘Birmingham City Football Club expresses its sincere gratitude to Tom Brady for his involvement with and unwavering support for the club over the last three years. It was truly amazing to have someone with Tom’s experience and passion associated with the club, and the club looks forward to continuing to build on that foundation from the training ground to the Birmingham community.’.

Chelsea have invited minority shareholders with their women’s team.

NBA star Giannis Antetokounmpo previously purchased a stake in the side, partnering with Alexis Ohanian, the founder of social media platform Reddit who likewise invested in the team in 2025.

Man City survive tunnel clash and Porto fury thanks to Haaland double

📅 08 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 26 min read (5244 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~26 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Erling Haaland revealed on the eve of this clash how he loves chopping firewood in his spare time – and his goals set alight Manchester City’s Champions League campaign on a fractious evening in Porto.
  • So much for the newly introduced group stage of the competition taking time to warm up.
  • It has been revealed that and City were not easing themselves back into European action either, they went full throttle at the start of a tough set of group games.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Erling Haaland revealed on the eve of this clash how he loves chopping firewood in his spare time – and his goals set alight Manchester City’s Champions League campaign on a fractious evening in Porto.

So much for the newly introduced group stage of the competition taking time to warm up. This clash was a hot-blooded, bitter contest that spilt over in the tunnel at half-time, with players getting separated and tempers rising.

It has been revealed that and City were not easing themselves back into European action either, they went full throttle at the start of a tough set of group games. With Enzo Maresca, it looks like it will be all-out attack to get the best out of this team.

They can look nervous at the back, particularly with the ball at Gianluigi Donnarumma’s feet, but have attacking weapons to hurt any team in this elite competition. This was a performance that their rivals will take note of.

“It was a complete performance on and off the ball for 95 minutes,” was Maresca’s assessment.

According to recent reports, city will certainly scare the traditional heavyweights with Haaland leading their attack and taking an axe to Porto’s defence like he does with logs in his back garden. It was his 58th and 59th goal in 59 games in the Champions League, with his latest an expertly directed header off a post and a calm side-footed finish.

NO MISTAKE from Erling Haaland this time 💪He's put Man City 1-0 up in Porto 🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/UpKOqQA49s.

There is an argument that Pep Guardiola could have achieved more in the Champions League, given City’s dominance in domestic football. They have been knocked out by Real Madrid in the last three seasons but this is a new City, different personnel and even a new look.

Industry observers note that they wore their black and yellow away kit, inspired by “Manchester’s iconic worker bee” according to Puma, and grafted their way to victory here. Non-stop running going forward, and scrapping with Porto, too.

The Portuguese champions were not happy with Marc Guéhi’s challenge on Gabri Veiga and claimed an elbow was used, with the row carrying on in the tunnel at half-time with security guards separating the players. Rúben Dias also appeared to nudge a Porto official on his way to the dressing room.

“I didn’t see anything but anyway, you can ask how many times you see me or my bench stand up? Zero, for 95 minutes. How many times do you see their bench? So...” Maresca added.

Only Dias and Haaland remain from the starting line-up from the Champions League triumph three years ago, so this is essentially a newly introduced team with a new manager.

Erling Haaland seals the deal in Porto 🤝🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/10xSTtZ8nw.

Industry observers note that phil Foden, on as a sub in that game, started at Estádio do Dragão after his horse Wreck It Ronnie defeated Najidi Storm, which started the Goodwood race with 1-33 odds and is now the shortest-priced loser in British racing history. The rest of the team are new to City’s challenge.

That includes Ayyoub Bouaddi, 18, who was part of a £320m midfield refresh following the departure of Rodri, who was named among the Ballon d’Or nominees a few hours before kick-off to highlight the experience and class City have lost.

In a recent development, bouaddi, who cost £81.4m from Lille, made a good start in his full debut. The Moroccan teenager is neat on the ball and gets around the pitch, with the next step being able to dominate games like his predecessor.

It has been revealed that “In his last game he lost two balls and stayed calm and was back in our box,” Maresca said. “This indicates how good he is because any player after two [poor] passes panics, but he is just 18. Erling, Rúben, Mateo [Kovacic], they can manage these kind of games better, but you don’t expect it from a guy of 18. I didn’t see him panic.”.

Sources indicate that by Bouaddi’s side in midfield was Enzo Fernández, who sought to drive forward into space when City counter-attacked. He was among the players who, along with Dias, were reminded of their Benfica history by the home fans.

Diogo Costa tends to be linked with a move to the Premier League every summer, but has been a one-club man for his career so far. But he revealed why clubs are looking at him with his first-half saves to deny Haaland and Rayan Cherki.

Porto’s legendary goalkeeper, Helton, was in the press box at half-time and would have been impressed with the saves, although he was not in his seat when Haaland scored the first goal, which came 94 seconds after the restart.

In a recent development, city had worked the ball around the penalty area, with Antoine Semenyo drawing out Costa before laying off to Fernández. Haaland’s header from the cross had such precision that the goalkeeper did not dive as it angled in off a post.

Still, Porto had their chances with Alberto Costa heading wide from a corner and William Gomes charging down a Donnarumma kick – with City’s most nervous moments coming when they passed around their back line.

Industry observers note that man City are living dangerously here! 🫣Donnarumma nearly gifts Porto an equaliser 😬 pic.twitter.com/otIfZTHmdn.

But Haaland sealed the win as the game ticked into stoppage time, finding the bottom corner from Rayan Aït-Nouri’s cutback.

“It was an amazing game against the champions of Portugal. We knew it would be a difficult fight, man against man, they are a top team,” Haaland mentioned. “They play amazing football. All the pressure, we have to deliver on the massive stage and that’s what we did. We controlled the whole first half, created chances.”.

For Maresca, the victory was also a challenge against Porto’s aggression, with the Italian coach adding: “I was very pleased. We know in this kind of game when you come here it’s always difficult or tricky. The environment, the way they grew up, it’s normal, but I think we dealt with that very good.”.

Top performance, Enzo 👊✨ pic.twitter.com/ds0f207tpS.

Man City have now won seven of their last eight opening matchdays in the UEFA Champions League 🔵Starting strong 💪 pic.twitter.com/CIjsMj4Dig.

Industry observers note that “I think we could have scored more goals, especially in the first half. We overall deserved the win and happy with the performance. If you think you can come to a place like this and play and not concede any chances, that is not realistic and it is normal. I am quite lucky as I have a squad of good players. It is a special competition and all the games are very difficult. He [Ayyoub Bouaddi] never panicked and was very good. The performance from him was unbelievable. I am happy to reunite with Enzo [Fernandez], who was very good.”.

In a recent development, 36 - Erling Haaland scored his 36th UEFA Champions League goal for Manchester City, equalling Sergio Agüero as joint-most for the Citizens in the competition.Inevitability. pic.twitter.com/HHbNadybxh.

“I am so happy with how my teammates have welcomed me into the club. They are not just great players but great human beings. The fans have been absolutely brilliant and this is a newly introduced step in my career. Erling [Haaland] is an animal, a beast. Every time I am on the pitch, I will look for him and look to assist him. He is an amazing human being and helped me settle in. I am happy Enzo [Maresca] did all he good to make the move happen. I am so grateful for everything he has done for me and my family.”.

5️⃣9️⃣ appearances 5️⃣9️⃣ goals@Erling's #UCL record 🤯 pic.twitter.com/v6IvpwC9vm.

It has been revealed that “Amazing game against the champions of Portugal. We knew it was going to be a tough game, they play amazing football. We had to deliver on the biggest stage and we did. We controlled the whole of the first half. We created a lot of chances. They pushed us for a good 25 minutes in the second half but we pulled through. These are the games we have to win. We have had a great start to the season.

Industry observers note that “He [Ayyoub Bouaddi] had a really good game and he has been amazing in training. I think we have a gem there. We have to learn and Enzo [Maresca] demands a lot from us. We demand a lot from each other. It was an unreal atmosphere so I hope Enzo is happy with that.”.

Recent findings suggest that the final whistle is blown and Manchester City begin their Champions League campaign with a 2-0 win in Porto. Erling Haaland’s double gives Enzo Maresca a victory in his first Champions League game in charge of Manchester City.

Recent findings suggest that enzo has two shots from range in quick succession, one from a free-kick. The free-kick goes just wide and the second is saved by D Costa.

Industry observers note that it has been an ill-tempered game and tempers have boiled over again. Rosario and Haaland are involved in a tussle on the floor, which then leads to a mass melee. Haaland and Rosario are both booked for their part in starting that. Haaland is pleased that he got booked but I am not sure why. Both played their part in that melee.

It has been revealed that enzo Maresca’s side will head home with all three points. Ait-Nouri’s cross from the left side of the box picks out Haaland, who first-time shot from 10 yards out picks out the far corner. A clinical finish from Haaland and Manchester City will start their Champions League campaign with a win.

Erling Haaland seals the deal in Porto 🤝🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/10xSTtZ8nw.

There will be five added minutes.

Sources indicate that that is really poor refereeing. Porto are denied two clear fouls before Rosario is then punished for a foul on Enzo, which was a foul but so too were the previous two incidents. Francesco Farioli is then booked for his protestations but you can understand their frustration.

Ait-Nouri has the chance to warp up the three points with an effort from the edge of the box but his shot with his weaker right foot goes narrowly wide.

Nothing comes from the corner as Hwang’s delivery to the front post is dreadful.

Haaland has his fourth headed chance of the game but this one goes over the bar from Ndiaye’s cross. Haaland has scored one of those chances but spurned some good ones.

Down the other end, Fofana, only just on, wins Porto a corner and whips up the home fans.

In a recent development, A final change of the night for Porto sees Fofana replace Veiga. One last roll of the dice from Francisco Farioli.

Sources indicate that whilst Manchester City’s lead is only 1-0, Porto will believe an equaliser is there for them. However, the momentum they were building 10/15 minutes ago has seemingly been lost and the visitors have managed to wrestle back a bit more control.

That is a major chance missed by Pepe. Gimenez receives it down the left and pings a cross to the back post. The cross perfectly picks out Pepe, who fluffs his lines and completely mis-kicks.

Industry observers note that manchester City are making their final two substitutions of the night as Kovacic and Ait-Nouri come on for Bouaddi and Foden. Ait-Nouri looks like he is going to play left wing.

Two more changes for Porto as Silva and M Fernandes are replaced by Gimenez and Moura.

In a recent development, porto are going to make their first two changes of the night as Hwang and former Norwich man Sainz come on. Varela and Gomes head off.

For the second time in the half, Donnarumma is lucky. To be fair to the Manchester City keeper, the pass back to him is poor but he is then fortunate. His attempted ball out to his left is intercepted by Gomes but it rolls behind for a goal kick. That ball could have rolled straight into the Manchester City net or fallen straight back at Gomes feet with an empty net ahead of him. Donnarumma was very lucky on Saturday against Coventry to avoid a calamitous moment and he is lucky to avoid another awful moment for the second time in quick succession.

Man City are living dangerously here! 🫣Donnarumma nearly gifts Porto an equaliser 😬 pic.twitter.com/otIfZTHmdn.

It has been revealed that ndiaye receives it out on the left before driving inside. He gets his shot away from the edge of the box and tries to pick out the far corner but it is too close to D Costa and an easy save for the Porto keeper.

A fine pass from Rosario inside his own half cuts through Manchester City’s midfield sends Varela racing through the Manchester City half. He plays it out to his right to find Gomes, who cuts inside onto his left before trying to beat Donnarumma at his near post but the shot goes wide.

Enzo Maresca responds to a shift in momentum in this game making a double change. Anderson and Ndiaye come on for Cherki and Semenyo.

Industry observers note that porto have started to gain some momentum and they want a penalty. Bouaddi is perhaps a touch fortunate not to be penalised for a foul right on the edge of the box but it may have been just outside the penalty area. You can feel the game starting to turn in Porto’s favour.

Varela is inches away from an equaliser for Porto and plenty of the home fans thought the ball was in the net. Varela sends a curling effort towards goal from the edge of the box but it goes narrowly wide.

It has been revealed that that was a glorious chance for Porto to equalise. A corner is sent in from the left to the back post, where Alberto heads it back across goal. However, none of his teammates, including Silva, could tap the ball into the net. Porto should probably be back on level terms.

Donnrumma is a very, very lucky man. Porto would have had a certain penalty as Donnarumma completely flattened Pepe but the latter was offside so it is no penalty. Donnarumma has been booked but avoids a penalty, which would have been a guarantee had Pepe been onside.

Just three minutes into the second half, Enzo Maresca has made a substitution. Gvardiol, on a yellow, is withdrawn and Khusanov is brought on.

Porto’s legendary goalkeeper, Helton, was embracing Daniel Sturridge in the press box and they weren’t in their seats when the goal went in. Lovely move from City and Haaland steered in his 58th goal in the competition.

Erling Haaland moves 7th in the ALL-TIME UCL top-scorers list 💪🇳🇴📊 pic.twitter.com/oIkrPxm0gT.

In a recent development, haaland wasted two headed opportunities in the first half but he does not spurn this chance. It is a first Manchester City assist for Enzo, who clips in a cross from the left side of the box. Haaland meets it and his header glances off the far post and goes in.

We are back under way in Porto. Tempers were really starting to boil over as that first half wore on so will that continue into the second half?

The former Liverpool, Manchester City and Chelsea striker has described the incident involving Marc Guehi and Gabri Veiga as a “nasty collision” and “it does not look good at all”. I think Guehi is a lucky man to still be on the pitch as some VAR officials would surely have recommended a review for that foul. Porto boss Francesco Farioli felt Guehi led with his elbow and the home fans were not happy with that as well as a number of other decisions in that first half.

The first half is brought to an end and tempers are flaring as the two sides head off, with the game level at 0-0 at the break. The Porto fans and players are not happy with the officiating and Enzo is also involved in some antics.

Sources indicate that gvardiol needs to be careful as he is not punished for delaying a restart when you consider he is already on a booking. The Porto fans want to see a second yellow but the referee notes the ball was moving so Porto could not take the restart.

Should Guehi be in trouble here? He appears in real time to win his header but when you watch the replays he led with his arm. He catches Veiga right in the face and Guehi could be in some strife. However, VAR is not going to take any further action and Guehi can count himself lucky. The medics are on to tend to Veiga and you do wonder why VAR has not recommended a review. The ridiculous thing about that was that Guehi was not punished with a yellow card or even a free-kick. That clearly indicates the referee did not properly see it.

Industry observers note that porto fans quick to remind Ruben Dias and Enzo Fernandez of their Benfica history. They jeered the pair when they got on the ball. Enzo is getting it from all angles at the moment, with Coventry fans taunting him at the weekend. He can expect more of that in the Premier League after his part in England’s exit at the World Cup, which led to Argentina players holding up a flag saying the Falkland Islands were Argentina’s.

Tensions are boiling over. They have been threatening to do so between Gomes and Gvardiol for a little while and now they do. Gomes steals the ball off Gvardiol and attempts to counter but is pulled back by Gvardiol, who is rightly booked. Gomes is not happy with Gvardiol and they come to blows.

D Costa twice denies Manchester City in a matter of seconds. First he saves from Haaland, then gets to his feet to deny Cherki. Manchester City are knocking on the door and you do feel like a goal is coming for Enzo Maresca’s side.

No goals in Porto but Real Madrid have their second at home against Inter Milan through Fede Valverde.

Manchester City struggled to carve out any genuine chances in the opening quarter of an hour but there are creating more and more opportunities, the latest falling to Foden, whose shot from the right side of the box looking for the far corner is saved by D Costa.

It is not often you see Haaland miss two good chances with his head in quick succession but that is what has happened. Semenyo cuts inside on the left onto his right and curls in a cross into a good area. He picks out Haaland but the Norwegian’s header misses the target. He knows he should have done better as he shakes his head in frustration.

Porto’s front three have struggled to have much of an impact in the game, in particular Silva up top, who has been almost non-existent.

In a recent development, A great save from D Costa to deny Haaland. Foden’s cross just before the byline on the left side of the box picks out Haaland. The Norwegian has barely touched the ball tonight but comes close to opening the scoring. However, D Costa is on hand to deny him with a fine save. Should Haaland have given D Costa the chance to save it? Maybe not.

In probably the marquee match-up of the night, Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid are taking on Inter Milan at the Bernabeu. Real have just taken the lead through Kylian Mbappe.

Semenyo cuts inside from the left and gets a shot away from the edge of the box but it is straight at D Costa. That was Manchester City’s first shot of the night.

In a recent development, veiga has a shot saved at the near post by Donnarumma but the offside flag goes up. Veiga and Pep exchange a neat one-two down Porto’s left before Veiga’s effort is saved but Pepe was offside in the build-up.

Manchester City are dominating possession and perhaps it was a ploy by Enzo Marecsa to take it slowly and hog the ball in order to take the early sting out of Porto. The visitors would have been expecting the hosts would want to start hot so maybe they were willing to be slow on the ball in order to quieten down the crowd early doors. They have not had a shot yet and not really threatened the Porto goal but the hosts have not offered much going forward.

The weather in Porto really is horrible, the type of weather you would expect in Manchester in mid-November than Porto in early September.

Industry observers note that porto have a strong defensive record thus far this season but undoubtedly they will be tested a lot more tonight than they are in Liga Portugal. You would also imagine they will have to be clinical in attack as they are unlikely to create as many chances as they do domestically.

It has been a positive start for Unai Emery’s Aston Villa out in Belgium as they lead Club Brugge 3-1 at half-time.

In a recent development, enzo Maresca takes charge of his first Champions League game in charge of Manchester City as they have travelled to Portugal to take on Porto at the Estadio do Dragao. These sides last met during the Champions League group stages during the 2020/21 season. Manchester City won 3-1 at home before the two sides drew 0-0 in this stadium.

Manchester City were busy late on in the transfer window, bringing in both Iliman Ndiaye and Enzo Fernandez as they spent nearly £200m on deadline day alone. They come into tonight’s game off the back of three straight Premier League victories to kick off the Maresca era. Maresca has limited Champions League experience as a manager, which came with Chelsea last season. Manchester City have won their opening game of a Champions League campaign in six of the last seven seasons but this will be the first time since 2015/16 that Manchester City embark on a Champions League campaign without Pep Guardiola at the helm.

Recent findings suggest that “It is a hard place to come [Porto],” remarked Maresca. “They have started really well. In the last 14/15 games in Europe they lost just one, that shows a difficult place to come, but we will try our best and try to win the game. It is a very, very good team. They have different players, but in terms of the team it is very clear in the way they play. They are aggressive without the ball and on the ball, they have a clear style. But we will try our best and try to win the game. The ambition is the same; try to be ourselves and to win games and then we will see.”.

Porto, managed by Francesco Farioli, have won every league game so far this season and already sit four points clear at the summit of Liga Portugal. Farioli takes charge of his first game as a manger in the Champions League and the club make their return to the elite European competition after two seasons away.

Industry observers note that “We are going to face one of the big favourites to win the competition,” Farioli said. “It will be a game that will demand that we be at our best, and we know that whenever we step onto the Dragão pitch, something special can happen. I am happy to be in the Champions League for the first time at 37 years old. This will be my first game, but we approach every game with the same attention to detail and the same focus. It is easy for the players to be motivated tomorrow [tonight]. But the key will be our strategy and our ability to execute it, individually and collectively.”.

Industry observers note that porto were in the Europa League last season, making it to the quarter-finals, where they were knocked out by Nottingham Forest 2-1 on aggregate. The omens would not appear to be on Porto’s side tonight; they have only won two of their last 16 games against English opposition in major European competition.

Très aguerries, les Amazones en passent 13 à Guéret

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Il y a des déplacements champêtres en Coupe de France qui ressemblent à des pièges (les Verts en savent quelque chose) mais celui des Amazones hier après-midi à Guéret à l'occasion du 1er tour fédéral, a plutôt ressemblé à une aimable promenade bucolique.Face aux féminines de l'ES Guérétoise (Régionale 2), les protégées de Yannick Chandioux ont transformé leur entrée en lice dans la compétition en véritable feu d'artifice avec un cinglant 13-0.Leader de Seconde Ligue, le coach stéphanois avait logiquement décidé de s'appuyer sur un onze largement remanié, tout en conservant suffisamment de cadres, tel qu'Ithaisa Viñoly, étonnamment préférée à Emma Templier, ainsi que Mathilde Kack ou Lorna Chicha Douvier.
  • It has been revealed that au-delà de la qualification, cette victoire restera dans les annales de la section féminine stéphanoise.

Il y a des déplacements champêtres en Coupe de France qui ressemblent à des pièges (les Verts en savent quelque chose) mais celui des Amazones hier après-midi à Guéret à l'occasion du 1er tour fédéral, a plutôt ressemblé à une aimable promenade bucolique.Face aux féminines de l'ES Guérétoise (Régionale 2), les protégées de Yannick Chandioux ont transformé leur entrée en lice dans la compétition en véritable feu d'artifice avec un cinglant 13-0.Leader de Seconde Ligue, le coach stéphanois avait logiquement décidé de s'appuyer sur un onze largement remanié, tout en conservant suffisamment de cadres, tel qu'Ithaisa Viñoly, étonnamment préférée à Emma Templier, ainsi que Mathilde Kack ou Lorna Chicha Douvier. La surprise du chef avait pour nom Jalia Chabourine, 20 ans, pour sa première titularisation en verte. Et le moins que l'on puisse dire, c'est que la jeune Francilienne n'aura pas traîné pour trouver la bonne carburation: dès la 7e minute, elle ouvrait le bal d'une tête bien placée, à la réception d'un service de Jana Zufankova (0-1) suivie par Héloïse Mansuy, capitaine d'un jour, à la 15e minute (0-2). Le temps que Dona Scannapieco loupe un penalty et le vrai festival commençait avec d'abord Lorna Chicha Douvier (0-3) puis un triplé de Jalia Chabourine en 5 minutes (23e, 25e, 28e). Un quadruplé express qui la plaçait en tête des buteuses de la saison avec Mansuy et Isgrig (5 buts). Dona Scannapieco ajoutait une 7e pierre à l'édifice à la 37e minute avant que Chabourine ne signe son cinquième but personnel à la 41e, faisant d'elle la meilleure réalisatrice de la saison ! Roxane Couasnon concluait cette première période totalement à sens unique à la 43e minute (0-9) avant que la mi-temps ne préserve les Guérétoises pendant un petit quart d'heure...Au retour des vestiaires, les Stéphanoises levaient légèrement le pied et ne marquaient plus que 4 buts par l'intermédiaire de Scannapieco (70e et 84e), Belhout-Achi (81e) et Chicha Douvier (89e) encore.On aura également noté l'apparition de la jeune Thaïs Aznar pour son troisième match pro, un an après le dernier en Coupe LFFP.

It has been revealed that au-delà de la qualification, cette victoire restera dans les annales de la section féminine stéphanoise. Avec treize buts inscrits, les Amazones signent le plus large succès officiel recensé de l'histoire de l'équipe. Yannick Chandioux: "Je suis satisfait de l’image que l’équipe a donnée. On a fait une bonne entame, ce qui nous a permis de marquer rapidement. C’est intéressant dans ce type de matchs (...) Je souhaite également féliciter Jalia Chabourine, qui a eu moins de temps de jeu depuis le début de saison et qui a réussi aujourd’hui à inscrire cinq buts (...) Notre objectif principal est de remonter en Arkema Première Ligue, mais si l’on peut faire un joli parcours en Coupe de France, c’est toujours bon à prendre. Si on a marqué l’histoire, c’est top. Ce n’est pas ce qui m’intéresse le plus aujourd’hui, mais c’est toujours sympathique de contribuer à établir de nouveaux records pour la section féminine.L'aventure en Coupe de France se poursuivra au deuxième tour fédéral face à Montauban (D3), qui a obtenu sa qualification en dominant Bayonne (7-1).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

Ajax moved into a clear second place in the Eredivisie with a routine 3-0 win against ADO Den Haag, as Feyenood slipped to fifth after losing to local rivals Excelsior.

Davy Klaassen took just three minutes to stroke home the opening goal for Ajax and added a second just before half-time.

By then ADO had been reduced to 10 men following the dismissal of Matteo Waem for hauling down Tolu Arakodare.

But there was a blow for Ajax ahead of next weekend’s visit to Feyenoord when Jorthy Mokio, scorer of the second goal, was taken off injured after an accidental collision with Sékou Sylla.

Feyenoord, who started the month top of the Eredivisie, suffered their first home defeat in the derby against Excelsior since 1980 to continue a slump in form that has seen them draw two and lose four of their last six games.

Givairo Read’s blistering shot gave Feyenoord the lead after just two minutes, but Excelsior were ahead by half-time and made it 3-1 when Casper Windell headed in a corner after 58 minutes. Despite an own goal by Jan Plug, on loan from Feyenoord, Excelsior were not to be denied.

PSV remain a point clear of Ajax at the top of the table after they cruised to a 4-1 win at NEC, with Filip Kostic opening the scoring with his first goal for PSV and his first Eredivisie goal since 2014, when he was playing for Groningen.

Utrecht sacked their managed Anthony Correia after just 14 matches after sinking to 15th place in the table with a 3-2 home defeat to Cambuur.

Correia won just four games after leaving Telstar, the club he led to promotion two seasons ago and where he spent his entire 15-year playing career. Youth team coach Mark Otten will take charge of the first team while Utrecht search for a replacement.

Willem II, searching for their first Eredivisie win in 30 matches, took a shock lead away to Twente despite being reduced to 10 men in the first half when Devin Haen was given space in the area to shoot past Joël Drommel.

The home side struggled to turn their superiority into goals, but an equaliser by Ramiz Zerrouki and a late header by Marko Pjaca gave them the points they needed to rise to third place above Feyenoord.

AZ also overtook Feyenoord as they beat Sparta 5-1 with a dominant second-half display, while Fortuna Sittard kept in touch with the leading group with a typically gritty 1-0 win at Go Ahead Eagles.

Go Ahead Eagles 0-1 Fortuna Sittard.

Sparta Rotterdam 1-5 AZ Alkmaar.

Twente Enschede 2-1 Willem II Tilburg.

Sous contrat avec l'ASSE jusqu'en 2029 mais prêté sans option d'achat au Pau FC, Luan Gadegbeku a hélas davantage joué en National 2 (151 minutes) qu'en Ligue 2 (147) depuis le début de saison !

Deux semaines après joué dans son intégralité le match que la réserve paloise a perdu (0-3) à Trélissac, le milieu de terrain de 19 ans était titulaire avant-hier contre Castanet. S'il a mangé une biscotte comme en Dordogne, le natif de Jusivy-sur-Orge (Essonne) a marqué le dernier but du succès (3-0) de son équipe avant de céder sa place à la 61e minute.

Il retrouvera cette même équipe de Castanet ce samedi en Haute-Garonne lors du 8e tour de Coupe de France. On lui souhaite de jouer l'intégralité de cette rencontre, comme lors de son précédent match dans cette compétition, facilement remporté 4-0 à Tarbes contre la modeste équipe de Lourdes (R1).

#108047. Industry News: Football's most involved mums after Cristiano Ronaldo outburst: The staunch and uncompromising negotiator, the one who still makes the bed and the celebrity charging for a meet-and-greet

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1237 w)

Industry News: Football's most involved mums after Cristiano Ronaldo outburst: The staunch and uncompromising negotiator, the one who still makes the bed and the celebrity charging for a meet-and-greet

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1237 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 02:00 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 04:21 EST, 21 November 2026.
  • Cristiano Ronaldo may have finally departed the international stage, but he still remained a major part of Portugal's story over the past week.
  • That came after they suffered a humiliating 4-1 defeat by Denmark in the first game since his retirement, their heaviest home loss in competitive history.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By WILL PICKWORTH, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 02:00 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 04:21 EST, 21 November 2026.

Cristiano Ronaldo may have finally departed the international stage, but he still remained a major part of Portugal's story over the past week.

That came after they suffered a humiliating 4-1 defeat by Denmark in the first game since his retirement, their heaviest home loss in competitive history.

In the aftermath of that match, Ronaldo's mother Dolores launched a furious and unprompted attack on the national team, claiming the defeat was just, and added she was happy to see the result.

Despite an emotional and historic tribute to Ronaldo pre-game, Dolores also expressed her unhappiness at what had unfolded, before she claimed the veteran's former international team-mates failed to show him the respect he deserved during his career.

Dolores has not always been an outspoken presence over the years, but has often stepped up to defend her son when she feels necessary.

So, in light of her outburst, Daily Mail Sport has taken a look at other examples of when the mums of footballers have got involved in their careers.

Cristiano Ronaldo's mum became embroiled in her son's row with Portugal's national team after saying she was happy to see them suffer a heavy defeat (Source: Instagram/doloresaveiroofficial).

Veronique Rabiot – Adrien Rabiot.

Adrien Rabiot's mother Veronique has developed a reputation as an uncompromising and fiercely protective negotiator in her role as his agent.

This has seen the French midfielder face several flashpoints in his career, beginning  when Veronique pulled him out of Man City's academy after just six months in 2008 because she felt they were not looking after his interests like they should be.

During his time at PSG, where Rabiot ultimately broke through and spent seven seasons in the first team, Veronique then frequently clashed with the club's hierarchy.

Potential transfers to Roma and Man United during his career have also both collapsed late on, a factor some reports attach to Veronique's role in the deals.

There have been several notable flashpoints on the international stage too, not least when she backed her son's controversial decision to withdraw from France's standby list for the 2018 World Cup.

But that was nothing compared to the aftermath of France's shock exit from Euro 2020 at the last-16 stage.

Veronique made headlines at the time for engaging in a heated confrontation with the parents of Kylian Mbappe and the entourage of Paul Pogba in the stands over on-pitch errors and perceived arrogance during Les Bleus' campaign.

Adrien Rabiot's mother Veronique (centre) has developed a reputation as a formidable force.

As the mother of one of the best footballers on the planet, Fayza Lamari was always likely to be a major powerbroker, and she has played a key role in Kylian Mbappe's career, acting as his chief negotiator and business manager.

This has seen Fayza oversee Mbappe's commercial obligations and image rights, while she played a central role in his dramatic contract extension at PSG in 2022.

Sources indicate that she was similarly important when Mbappe joined Real Madrid in 2024. On that occasion, she was credited for helping to secure a huge signing bonus and favourable image rights split for her son.

Fayza hasn't been afraid to publicly stand up for the forward, and she was key in the legal dispute over unpaid salary and bonuses that he felt he was owed by PSG after his exit.

PSG were ultimately ordered to pay Mbappe €60million (£52.5m) by a French court in a major victory for Fayza.

Kylian Mbappe's mum Fayza (also pictured with his brother Ethan) has played a key role in the commercial side of his career.

Sheila Ebana has been a foundational and supportive presence throughout Lamine Yamal's childhood and rise into professional football.

But, alongside regularly attending Yamal's games, Sheila has become a celebrity in her own right after embracing her public profile.

She regularly provides an insight into her life and shares behind the scenes clips with Yamal and his half brother Keyne on social media, racking up 2.8million followers on Instagram and 2.6million on TikTok.

Sheila has also regularly made paid appearances and attended VIP events, including a bizarre Christmas gala dinner that Daily Mail Sport went to in November 2025 where members of the public paid hundreds of pounds for a three-course meal, champagne, entertainment and a meet-and-greet.

To demonstrate how Sheila has embraced her fame, she once responded to online critics by retorting: 'I don't just think I'm famous - I am.'.

Lamine Yamal's mum (pictured below together with his half-brother Keyne) has embraced her celebrity fame.

Denise Bellingham – Jude Bellingham.

Jude Bellingham has often credited his mother Denise for helping to manage his life off the pitch and keep him grounded.

When he moved to Germany to join Borussia Dortmund as a 17-year-old, Denise went with him – before subsequently following the midfielder to Spain after his transfer to Real Madrid – while his father Mark stayed with his brother Jobe.

She is understood to handle his domestic affairs and finances, while Bellingham inadvertently revealed during the 2022 World Cup that she still made his bed.

Denise has generally provided a constant source of advice, logistical support – which has included driving him to training in the past – and organisational help throughout his time in the game.

The England star is clearly appreciative of all she has done, describing her as his 'queen' and 'backbone', and crediting her with helping to keep him level headed throughout the highs and lows of his career.

Jude Bellingham (pictured also with dad Mark and brother Jobe) has described his mum Denise as his 'queen' and 'backbone'.

Marcia Lewis – Myles Lewis-Skelly.

Myles Lewis-Skelly's mother Marcia Lewis has played a crucial role in his rise into Arsenal and England's first team.

When Lewis-Skelly entered the Arsenal academy system at the age of eight, Marcia wanted to learn more about football to ensure she could protect and guide her son's progression.

She subsequently qualified as an agent, meaning she now represents Lewis-Skelly, and also enrolled in a Master's degree in Football Business.

Marcia has since taken part in contract negotiations and filtered external pressures away from her son during his development.

She was later inspired to set up the No1Fan.club, a platform that aims to support families who have children in academy football.

The outlet is dedicated to helping navigate various challenges that arise, such as dealing with scouts, agents and the general pressures associated with youth football.

Myles Lewis-Skelly's mum Marcia Lewis tried to learn more about the business of football so she would be able to support her son on his journey (Source: Instagram/myleslewisskelly).

Harry Maguire's mother Zoe has taken a more low-profile approach to her son's career than others, yet she has never been afraid to speak out when she feels the need to.

This included back in 2023 when she snapped after years of watching her son face significant abuse, both online and in stadiums.

At the time, Zoe labelled the heat on the defender as 'disgraceful' and 'unacceptable', and mentioned it went 'far beyond' football.

She re-emerged into the public eye three years later when Maguire was snubbed from England's World Cup squad.

After that, she tweeted: 'Absolutely disgusted.'.

In another post addressing Maguire, she added: 'You couldn’t have done anymore. Hold your head high …Disgraceful.'.

Mac Allister not so sad now after Liverpool comeback winner

📅 09 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 27 min read (5489 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~27 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Do your talking on the pitch, as the old adage goes, and Alexis Mac Allister emphatically did just that as Liverpool came from behind to thrillingly win their first Champions League tie under fresh head coach Andoni Iraola in what was his debut at this level.
  • In a recent development, on the eve of this encounter, against a strong Atlético Madrid, one of the clubs who have recently tried to sign him, Mac Allister had spoken of his sadness.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Do your talking on the pitch, as the old adage goes, and Alexis Mac Allister emphatically did just that as Liverpool came from behind to thrillingly win their first Champions League tie under fresh head coach Andoni Iraola in what was his debut at this level.

In a recent development, on the eve of this encounter, against a strong Atlético Madrid, one of the clubs who have recently tried to sign him, Mac Allister had spoken of his sadness. Sadness that, unlike fellow midfielders Dominik Szoboszlai – Liverpool’s other scorer here – and Ryan Gravenberch, he had not been offered and signed a new contract.

Sources indicate that so, earn it. And many more goals – and overall performances like this – there is no doubt the Argentinian will have a deal placed in front of him. He scored with an arresting second-half shot, which proved to be the winner, and the smile across his face noted it all. Not so sad now as he was later substituted to a standing ovation with Gravenberch taking his place.

The goal came early in the second half, with Iraola attributing that to adjusting his tactics after being flummoxed by Atlético’s back five and packed midfield in a first half when Liverpool were second best.

Mac Allister was heavily involved through the build-up, eventually picking out Rio Ngumoha on the left whose shot was blocked and pinballed around. It dropped to Mac Allister, 20 yards out, and he hit the kind of unerring drive that gives the goalkeeper no chance. And so it proved. Boom. And Anfield was bouncing.

Mac Allister FIRES Liverpool into the lead at Anfield! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/KGOvuAEU4W.

There are certainly signs under Iraola, and following a difficult last campaign, that Mac Allister is beginning to rediscover the form he revealed during his first two seasons at Liverpool. Time and again the 27-year-old made vital interventions, showed aggression and walked the tightrope of a harsh early yellow card. He dovetailed with Szoboszlai and that might be a concern for Gravenberch – watched by the Netherlands’ new head coach Xavi Hernández – if Iraola persists with this approach.

Although Mac Allister has two years left on his current deal, the last thing Liverpool need is yet another attention-sapping contract saga, even if he is not the same scale of player as Mohamed Salah or Trent Alexander-Arnold.

In a recent development, for Iraola, after three Premier League games, comprising two draws and a victory over newly-promoted Ipswich Town, this will hopefully be lift off. A big European night at Anfield and coming from behind to beat one of the continent’s heavyweights.

It has been revealed that “I loved it,” Iraola remarked, before castigating himself for misreading the way Atlético would line up. And what of Mac Allister’s riposte? There was a smile from Iraola before the Spaniard’s usual diplomacy kicked in as he talked about a “lovely, lovely goal” and how good it was for his midfielders to contribute.

Liverpool had to fight for it and what will have satisfied Iraola is that the defence, which has come under such scrutiny, held out. Even so, there are still serious concerns over the suitability of Milos Kerkez at left-back – who was badly at fault for Atlético’s goal – although the robust Ronald Araújo showed he can be a strong and versatile option on the other flank. The Uruguayan, signed on loan from Barcelona, is such a presence in both penalty areas and has the capacity to gain cult status.

Recent findings suggest that as does £123m signing from Paris St-Germain Bradley Barcola, who should have scored – once, certainly, possibly twice – and possesses astonishing pace that will undoubtedly lead to goals. There are also encouraging signs that his presence could enliven Florian Wirtz. Barcola eventually also went off, but thankfully it was only to cramp.

There was a collective intake of breath across the Kop when Marcos Llorente was played through and bore down on them to give Atlético the lead. There was a desperate hope that he had strayed offside. There was then a realisation that Kerkez had, however, played him on with an appalling lack of awareness. Llorente beat Alisson.

According to recent reports, it owed much to a wonderful shimmy, deceiving Szoboszlai in centre field, by Julián Alvarez before he smartly threaded the ball through, and Mac Allister’s international team-mate almost doubled Atlético’s advantage soon after. Only to be denied by Alisson.

Llorente breaks the deadlock! 🔥That's now FIVE Champions League goals for the Atletico man against Liverpool at Anfield 🤯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Rxp4zurfpc.

According to recent reports, we knew, we feared it would be Llorente who scored. Remarkably, he has now half of his 10 goals in this competition against Liverpool. Indeed, he named his dog Anfield after his extra-time brace knocked Liverpool, then the holders, out in the last 16 in 2020. And Liverpool had made a dog’s dinner of defending this time.

This is a different Atlético. A far less defensive, far more expansive Atlético. In years gone by, once they were 1-0 it was game over under Diego Simeone. But these days they try and play more and that gives their opponents a chance. And so it proved.

Industry observers note that atlético goalkeeper Jan Oblak did well to deny Barcola, with his trailing foot, before Wirtz won the ball back and found Szoboszlai who eventually ended the movement. It owed much, however, to a clever backheel to pick out the midfielder who finished low into the corner. Who executed that backheel? That would be Araújo.

It has been revealed that szoboszlai slots home after a brilliant flick from Araujo! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UrHQTwtgsY.

Barcola should have scored, sent clear by Wirtz in a brilliant, sweeping counter-attack, before Mac Allister did.

The question now was whether Liverpool would show the resilience to see through the result. As Iraola made changes, they answered that with a resounding yes, which will have pleased him as much as the result, as much as the comeback, as much as Mac Allister’s stunning response.

It has been revealed that “I was enjoying it [the Anfield crowd]. They [Atletico Madrid] are a very good team. Technically, in the middle, lovely players. It is not easy to press those players as they have quality. They have been playing together forever. We find another comeback after Nottingham Forest, after Newcastle. We still have this thing to improve in the beginning of the games, but I am happy as we have shown some character. This is the Champions League, you do not have easy games.”.

"You can see he's football mad." ⚽Steven Gerrard on Andoni Iraola's passion and the impact he's making at Liverpool 👏🎙️ @laura_woodsy | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/M3qKhxt8HE.

It has been revealed that andoni Iraola has been speaking to TNT Sports and has confirmed that it was just cramp for the likes of Bradley Barcola, rather than an injury. Milos Kerkez also went off late with what appears to be just cramp.

Atletico had more possession in the second half but Liverpool were much the better side after the break.

"We can achieve everything we want." 💪Dominik Szoboszlai full of belief after Liverpool's Champions League victory over Atletico Madrid 👀🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ebSvagW4yx.

Sources indicate that there is the final whistle at Anfield and Liverpool start their Champions League campaign with a 2-1 win over Atletico Madrid. Liverpool did fall behind to Marcos Llorente’s goal but goals from Dominik Szoboszlai and Alexis Mac Allister give Andoni Iraola a win in his first Champions League game as a manager.

Victory in MD1 🤩 #UCL pic.twitter.com/SWFFhSudFJ.

First Champions League game. First Champions League win for Andoni Iraola ✅ pic.twitter.com/D3CE6w6V0b.

Koumas is tripped by Le Normand and that should be it.

That is a silly foul from Lookman, with Frimpong inside his own box running back towards his own goal, but Lookman decides to push him in the back.

Just 60 seconds remain at Anfield.

There will be five added minutes.

Liverpool think they have sealed it through Frimpong but the offside flag has gone up. First Munoz cuts onto his right and has a shot saved by Oblak. The ball falls to Frimpong, who slots home but he was clearly offside when Munoz took the initial shot.

Recent findings suggest that kerkez is currently down with cramp and his night is done. He will be replaced by Tsimikas and Liverpool will make their final change at the same time. Koumas comes on for Isak.

Atletico win a corner but it all stems from sloppy play in the centre of the pitch from Gravenberch. He has had a few sloppy moments since coming on.

The corner is flicked on by Hjulmand but ends up coming to nothing.

It isn’t the headline making performance, by any means, but that shouldn’t dilute the importance of Ronald Araujo’s contribution for Liverpool tonight and, indeed, against Ipswich last Friday. He’s doing what Liverpool wanted him to, providing versatility and leadership in their back four and - more than anything - quality. He hasn’t put a foot wrong.

Sources indicate that atletico win a corner out on the left in front of their travelling supporters. Grimaldo’s outswinger is flicked on by the head of Hancko at the near post but it goes over.

Isak has the chance to potentially seal the victory for Liverpool but Le Normand makes a crucial block. Le Normand has only just come on but already made a couple of defensive actions.

Liverpool win a corner out on the left with the last touch coming off Pubill, who was marking Van Dijk from a free-kick. Szoboszlai’s inswinger is headed away by Le Normand.

Digeo Simeone is making his final two substitutions of the night as Le Normand and Hjulmad replace Romero and Barrios,.

Atletico bring on David, on loan from Juventus, for Baena.

Alvarez has a chance inside the Liverpool box but his shot is straight at Alisson. There are some appeals for handball but it hit Munoz from such close range that it is never a penalty.

It has been revealed that liverpool are making a substitution as Mac Allister, who scored the goal to put Liverpool in front, is replaced by Gravenberch. Mac Allister, who made some comments in the press conference yesterday about his sadness at not being offered a latest contract, put in a good performance in the centre of Liverpool’s midfield. He was on a booking though so probably sensible to take him off when you can guarantee that the Atletico players would have tried to get him sent off.

Recent findings suggest that we’ll see what happens in the coming weeks and months but there have been glimmers here with Florian Wirtz looking better than he has done with pace to pass to; if it clicks with him, Bradley Barcola & Alexander Isak it could be exciting but one game must be built on. It’s frustrating that Barcola’s night has ended with what appears to be cramp or tightness in his calf because he was getting more joy than he had done before half-time. The massive challenge for Liverpool, too, is whether they have the nous to see this contest out.

The fresh Netherlands boss Xavi is in attendance at Anfield tonight, watching the likes of Van Dijk, Frimpong and Gravenberch, although the latter is still yet to come off the Liverpool bench.

Recent findings suggest that this is a concern for Liverpool. Barcola has gone down and seems to have some pain in his left calf. Is it cramp or an injury? It will be a double change for the home side as Frimpong and Munoz come on. Barcola is given a standing ovation as he goes off and the Liverpool fans will be hoping it is just cramp. Ngumoha also heads off.

Sources indicate that diego Simeone is going to make his first two changes of the night. Grimaldo and Lookman come on.

It is all Liverpool as they sense a third goal is there for the taking. Ngumoha does well down Liverpool’s left and pushes it past Pubill, who slides in and takes him down. Pubill is booked. He cannot believe it but I do not know why; a clear foul and yellow card.

In a recent development, that is a stunning strike from the Argentine. The ball falls to the midfielder just outside the box and he hits it first time. He hits the ball so crisply and there is nothing Oblak can do to stop it. Liverpool should have taken the lead through Barcola moments before they do now have the lead for the first time tonight.

Sources indicate that mac Allister FIRES Liverpool into the lead at Anfield! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/KGOvuAEU4W.

According to recent reports, well, that’s one way to prove you might warrant a newly introduced contract. A quite beautiful left footed drive from Alexis Mac Allister gives Liverpool the lead and it has been noticeable thus far in Andoni Iraola’s matches that his team get stronger at the start of the second period. Diego Simeone most wonder how Atleti are losing a game they were controlling but Liverpool’s speed on the break is proving very good at causing chaos.

Barcola should have his first Liverpool goal and the hosts should be ahead but the Frenchman misses the target. It is the perfect counter-attack really from Liverpool and it is Wirtz and Barcola who exchange passes from deep inside their own half all the way to the Atletico penalty area. Barcola drives forward, into the Atletico box, and you think he is going to slot it into the bottom corner but his effort goes just wide. Barcola could and perhaps should have a brace tonight.

Barcola wins the first corner of this second half off Hancko right in front of The Kop. Liverpol take it short before Mac Allister clips the ball in. Araujo meets it and his header is powerful but it is off target.

In a recent development, we are back under way at Anfield. No changes from either side at the break.

Some of the statistics are pretty even but Atletico Madrid have had just three touches in the Liverpool penalty area, yet have a goal to their name.

Recent findings suggest that the first half at Anfield is brought to an end and it is level at 1-1 at the break. Llorente gave Atletico the lead before Szoboszlai equalised for Liverpool. The home fans let the officials know what they think of their performance in that first half.

One added minute at the end of this first half.

There has been about five minutes of squabbling between the Liverpool and Atletico benches, so much so that Tommy Elphick - Andoni Iraola’s assistant - missed Dominik Szoboszlai score the equaliser. Tensions have only increased after a nasty little challenge from Cristian Romero on Alexander Isak. The half-time whistle might be coming at a good time to defuse the situation but you fancy the walk back to the dressing rooms will be spicy.

In a recent development, the conduct of the Atletico players is frankly embarrassing, not a massive surprise from a Diego Simeone side. Kang goes down clutching his face when there was barely any contact and then, unlike Isak, he does not have to spend a minute off the pitch.

Recent findings suggest that isak is on the ground, clutching at his knee, after a heavy challenge from Romero. It is a nasty challenge from Romero, who remarkably is neither booked nor penalised. To compound the awful officiating, Isak now has to spend a minute off the pitch owing to the new rules. What do you make of that new rule of the player who is down going off for a minute? Have your say in the comments section at the bottom of the blog.

Moments after Liverpool equalised, Atletico have a decent opportunity to restore their lead but Baena drags his effort wide from the edge of the box.

According to recent reports, moments after Barcola could not take a massive chance to equalise for Liverpool, Szoboslzai does. First, Barcola is denied by Oblak. Liverpool keep it alive inside the Atletico box and a simple sensational flick by Aruajo finds Szoboszlai, who finds the bottom corner with a clinical finish. Kerkez has been poor tonight but he deserves credit for his part in that goal as he was the player to initially win it back for Liverpool with a good press.

Szoboszlai slots home after a brilliant flick from Araujo! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UrHQTwtgsY.

Industry observers note that liverpool look like a team that has been out of the Champions League for a couple of years and are only just finding its feet, which seems strange given they missed only one year in the last 10. They have glimmers of promise but they aren’t convincing anyone they will blow Atleti’s house down. One day everything will align for Atleti and they will reach another final. They have an outside chance this year, especially if Julian Alvarez - easily the best player on this pitch - has anything to do with it. Diego Simeone always has class strikers at the top of his team and Alvarez stands comparison with any who have gone before.

Wirtz has a great chance to equalise for Liverpool but his shot on the half volley is saved by Oblak. It would not have mattered anyway had the ball ended up in the net because Isak was offside before crossing for Wirtz.

Sources indicate that some of the officiating tonight has been appalling and the latest example is VAR taking a check on a possible red card for Mac Allister for a foul that is never a red card in a million years. The officials then take an age to give yet another obvious offside and, in the end, the referee gives it rather than the linesman. That really does sum up the officials tonight as the referee should not be the one to give offsides.

According to recent reports, alvarez shoots from distance and forces Alisson into a good save diving to his right. There was a suspicion of offside from Simeone in the build-up.

Atletico take it short but Simeone’s shot is blocked by Araujo.

Recent findings suggest that what a save from Alisson! 🤯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/PuajED3Rks.

The Anfield faithful are furious. Two fouls in quick succession are not given when they were both clearly fouls. The referee appears to have a different interpretation of body checks and taking people out off the ball than the rest of us.

The Spanish side take the lead at Anfield and it is another goal on this ground for Llorente. Alvarez feeds a through ball to pick out the run of Llorente, who is onside. He takes one touch before firing past Alisson from the edge of the box. That is poor, poor defending from Kerkez, who not only played Llorente onside but then did not track the run properly. Llorente now has five goals on this ground.

Llorente breaks the deadlock! 🔥That's now FIVE Champions League goals for the Atletico man against Liverpool at Anfield 🤯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Rxp4zurfpc.

The idea that Atletico Madrid are focused on spoiling and nullifying belongs in the past. They are an attractive team, well organised and you suspect they have the gears to cause Liverpool problems... and as we type, they have just opened the scoring by playing straight through Liverpool’s middle. It was a bad goal for home side to concede. Milos Kerkez was out of sync with the rest of Liverpool’s defence and Marcos Llorente has galloped straight through. As we remarked at the start: it’s a big test for the hosts... it’s just got even bigger.

A little line about Llorente, who has now scored five times against Liverpool in the Champions League. He is fond of playing in this arena, he named his dog “Anfield! when he bought it in 2021.

According to recent reports, chance for Barcola. Szoboszlai clips a lovely ball in behind down the right channel to pick out the run of Barcola. The Frenchman takes it down beautifully before having his shot saved by Oblak. Barcola’s best moment thus far tonight.

Baena takes a first-time effort on from a central position around 25 yards out but he cannot keep his effort down and it sails into The Kop.

Atletico were renowned for years under Diego Simeone is being very tight at the back and in midfield, especially away from home. However, in recent years they have become more expansive and as a result are more open.

According to recent reports, liverpool win their first corner of the night at the Anfield Road End in front of the travelling Atletico fans. They take it short and Szoboslzai takes it towards the Atletico box. It appeared to be a very obvious foul on Szoboszlai right on the edge of the box but nothing is given. At the very least, it should have been given a free-kick as there was definitely at least one foul.

Barcola, who has won the Champions League with PSG in the last two seasons, is starting out on the right for Liverpool tonight with Ngumoha on the left.

Significant test for Liverpool and it will be fascinating to see how this formation works out. It looks very much like it is 4-4-2, with Florian Wirtz almost alongside Alexander Isak and Rio Ngumoha the left winger and Bradley Barcola on the opposite flank - a position Andoni Iraola has referenced him playing in Lyon as a teenager. It’s also a big test for Iraola against Diego Simeone, the wily and vastly experienced manager, who is immaculately dressed - as always - in his trademark black suit.

Liverpool have a chance inside the opening minute. Szoboszlai wins it inside his own half and drives forward. He then plays it out to his right to find Isak, whose shot from the right side of the box is dragged wide of the far post. Isak did score from a similar position against Ipswich last Friday, when he scored at the near post.

A minute’s silence to remember the victims of the landslides in Nepal is impeccably observed.

We are under way at Anfield. Liverpool’s Champions League campaign gets going as Andoni Iraola takes charge of his first game as a manager in this competition.

It has been revealed that the two sides emerge from the tunnel to a cacophony of noise and we are moments away from kick-off at Anfield. The home fans boo the Champions League anthem and belt out “Liverpool! Liverpool!” over the top of it. Here is a reminder of how the two sides line up this evening:.
